title: 二十八个木衣夹  (Twenty-Eight Wooden Clothespins)

segments.t: At the front desk, Chen unties a canvas drawstring bag and pours three dozen smooth birch-wood clothespins onto the blotter before Qing and Zhou. Let us listen in first.
老陈，木头晾衣夹？！咱们是办周年茶会，又不是晾床单！
周经理，等一下——你看这原色桦木做得多光滑、多干净！
看我用深色木工铅笔在平的那一面写上“一号”会怎样。
原木上的铅笔字碰水绝对不晕，还能牢牢夹住折好的布餐巾！
等一等……一面写桌号，另一面写客人名字，再夹到厚亚麻布上？！
而且每人都能把自己的木衣夹夹在茶碟边或口袋上留作纪念！
老陈、小晴——这主意既雅致质朴又防风，而且一分钱都不用多花！
再说，我账本第四十页上还工工整整抄了一份完整备份名单呢。
周经理，你按顺序念名字，我把一号到二十八号衣夹写出来！
一号夹：八号房的尊贵老地图师！二号夹：宋老师！
看小晴写得多麻利——半条街的名字都已经排成整齐的木夹队列了。
端着这篮子出去，让下午的微风检验一下咱们的防风餐桌吧！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
老陈，木头晾衣夹？！咱们是办周年茶会，又不是晾床单！

'Wooden laundry clothespins, Chen?! We're hosting an anniversary tea, not hanging bedsheets!' Compound "liangyijia" pairs "liang" ("air-dry") with "yijia" ("clothes clip"), while "you bu shi" playfully protests "it's not as if we're..."
周经理，等一下——你看这原色桦木做得多光滑、多干净！

'Hold on a second, Zhou—look how smooth and clean this natural birch wood is!' "Yuanse" describes unpainted, natural material color ("yuan" = original + "se" = color), and paired "duo ... duo ..." exclaims "how very...!"
看我用深色木工铅笔在平的那一面写上“一号”会怎样。

'Watch what happens when I write Number One in dark carpenter pencil along the flat side.' In "xieshang 'yihao'", attaching "shang" after "xie" ("write") expresses putting the label ("yihao", Number One) neatly onto the surface.
原木上的铅笔字碰水绝对不晕，还能牢牢夹住折好的布餐巾！

'Pencil writing on bare wood never smudges in water, and it clips tightly onto a folded cloth napkin!' "Juedui bu yun" insists it will absolutely never bleed, while "laolao jiazhu" emphasizes a firm, unshakeable grip ("laolao").
等一等……一面写桌号，另一面写客人名字，再夹到厚亚麻布上？！

'Wait a moment... table number on one side, guest name on the other side, clipped to thick linen?!' Splitting "yimian" (one side) against "ling yimian" (the other side) neatly maps both flat faces of each wooden pin.
而且每人都能把自己的木衣夹夹在茶碟边或口袋上留作纪念！

'And everyone can clip their wooden clothespin onto a saucer rim or pocket as a keepsake!' "Liuzuo jinian" means to keep something as a memento ("jinian"), and "chadie bian" points to the rim of a tea saucer.
老陈、小晴——这主意既雅致质朴又防风，而且一分钱都不用多花！

'Chen, Qing—this idea is charming, rustic, windproof, and doesn't cost a single extra cent!' "Ji ... you ..." stacks up the praises ("both charming and windproof"), while "yi fen qian dou buyong duo hua" means "not one cent extra."
再说，我账本第四十页上还工工整整抄了一份完整备份名单呢。

'Besides, I also have a complete backup list copied neatly on page forty of my ledger.' "Zaishuo" introduces a reassuring bonus point ("besides"), and four-character "gonggong zhengzheng" praises neat, disciplined handwriting.
周经理，你按顺序念名字，我把一号到二十八号衣夹写出来！

'Read the names out in order, Zhou, while I write out clothespins one through twenty-eight!' "An shunxu" means "following the proper order," and "xie chulai" indicates producing each numbered clip one after another.
一号夹：八号房的尊贵老地图师！二号夹：宋老师！
'Pin Number One: our honored mapmaker from Room Eight! Pin Number Two: Song!' Respectful "zungui" means "honored" or "esteemed," fitting Zhou's theatrical announcement of "yihao jia" (Clip One).
看小晴写得多麻利——半条街的名字都已经排成整齐的木夹队列了。

'Look how briskly Qing writes—half the street's names are already lined up in neat wooden rows.' Brisk compliment "mali" describes quick, nimble hands at work, while "paicheng" means arranged cleanly into rows.
端着这篮子出去，让下午的微风检验一下咱们的防风餐桌吧！

'Carry this basket outside and let the afternoon breeze test out our windproof tables!' A light breeze is "weifeng" ("tiny wind"), and "jianyan yixia" playfully turns the afternoon gust into an official inspector.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

一号夹：八号房的尊贵老地图师！二号夹：宋老师！
看小晴写得多麻利——半条街的名字都已经排成整齐的木夹队列了。

Humble birch clothespins and dark carpenter pencil turn a soggy poster disaster into windproof courtyard keepsakes! See you next time.
明天见！
